subject: Deckent competitive proximity
calculation: weighted arithmetic mean of dimension scores
rounding: two decimals in data; one decimal in narrative tables

dimensions.label: Buyer/job overlap
dimensions.definition: The same buyer can choose this product instead of Deckent for the same operating job.

dimensions.label: Orchestration authority
dimensions.definition: Depth of canonical planning, delegation, dependency, attempt and settlement control.

dimensions.label: Governance, approvals and audit
dimensions.definition: Policy enforcement, approvals, identity, budgets, audit and least-authority controls.

dimensions.label: Durability and recovery
dimensions.definition: Crash survival, checkpoints, replay, fencing, idempotency and recovery semantics.

dimensions.label: Provider/runtime neutrality
dimensions.definition: Ability to host or govern heterogeneous agents, providers and execution environments.

dimensions.label: Memory, learning and evaluation
dimensions.definition: Persistent memory plus evidence-grounded evaluation, adaptation and promotion.

dimensions.label: Product surfaces and operator UX
dimensions.definition: Terminal, desktop, IDE, web, mobile, connectors and supervision usability.

dimensions.label: Multi-tenancy, enterprise and scale
dimensions.definition: Tenant isolation, admin controls, deployment breadth and credible scale posture.

classification_rule.direct_core: proximity >= 7.00 AND buyer_job_overlap >= 7.00 AND a runnable operator/control-plane product exists
classification_rule.platform_substitute: can compress Deckent's value into an incumbent platform, but is provider- or domain-bound
classification_rule.structural_adjacent: high technical overlap but sold/used primarily as a framework or infrastructure building block
classification_rule.product_adjacent: overlaps one or more surfaces or tasks without replacing Deckent's control-plane job
classification_rule.not_direct: useful reference, complement or integration target rather than a current Deckent substitute

rows.name: Naive
rows.closest_because: Governed multi-tenant agent profiles, durable teams, budgets, approvals, audit, memory and Agent IaC form a real Agent OS/control-plane substitute.
rows.farther_because: Hosted regulated business rails are the center of gravity; local-first cross-environment verified software execution is not.

rows.name: Ruflo
rows.closest_because: A broad agent meta-harness with swarms, routing, memory, learning, plugins and Codex/Claude integration attacks Deckent's orchestration and learning story directly.
rows.farther_because: Outcome provenance and enterprise authority are weaker; prior source audit found caller-supplied optimistic success entering adaptation.

rows.name: Cline
rows.closest_because: CLI, IDEs, Kanban worktrees, SDK, teams, schedules, connectors, plugins and enterprise controls converge on Deckent's product breadth.
rows.farther_because: The public contract is still coding-agent centered and does not expose Deckent-like canonical evidence settlement or governed learning.

rows.name: GitHub Agent HQ + Agentic Workflows
rows.closest_because: Multi-agent mission control plus repository-native, sandboxed, policy-controlled automation can absorb Deckent's engineering buyer job.
rows.farther_because: It is GitHub/SDLC-centric rather than a local-first, domain-general Agent OS with a closed verified-learning kernel.

rows.name: Paperclip
rows.closest_because: A provider-neutral multi-company control plane with goals, org charts, budgets, approvals, heartbeats and audit targets the autonomous-company operating job.
rows.farther_because: Paperclip explicitly remains a control plane rather than an execution plane; verified outcomes and organizational learning are not its current center.

rows.name: stablyai/orca
rows.closest_because: A polished cross-platform fleet workbench with worktrees and durable orchestration is the strongest productized operator-UX substitute.
rows.farther_because: Verified outcome evaluation, closed learning and organization-grade policy depth remain visibly thinner.

rows.name: LangGraph + LangSmith
rows.closest_because: Durable execution, persistence, human interrupts, tracing and evaluation overlap strongly with Deckent's kernel concerns.
rows.farther_because: It is a developer runtime/platform used to build agent products, not an opinionated operator-facing Agent OS replacement.

rows.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
rows.closest_because: Typed workflows, checkpointing, multi-agent patterns, memory and Azure enterprise integration cover many Deckent primitives.
rows.farther_because: It is primarily an SDK/framework and Azure ecosystem building block rather than a full operator control plane.

rows.name: CrewAI + AMP
rows.closest_because: Crews, flows, persisted state, guardrails, HITL, observability and managed deployment resemble a production agent platform.
rows.farther_because: Teams embed CrewAI to build automations; AMP does not yet replace Deckent's full local operator and heterogeneous coding-runtime control job.

rows.name: OpenAI Codex
rows.closest_because: Local/cloud tasks, subagents, worktrees, app-server, SDK, approvals, sandbox, automations and enterprise policy compress many Deckent surfaces into the host platform.
rows.farther_because: It is an OpenAI-native coding agent, not a provider-neutral multi-runtime organization control plane with independent outcome governance.

rows.name: OpenClaw
rows.closest_because: Gateway, isolated agents, cross-channel routing, schedules and shared exec approvals pressure Deckent's multi-surface runtime.
rows.farther_because: Official security documentation treats gateway and node as one operator trust domain, not hostile multi-tenant isolation.

rows.name: Claude Code
rows.closest_because: Subagents, agent teams, hooks, checkpoints, SDK and managed enterprise settings can remove the need for a separate coding orchestrator.
rows.farther_because: Provider-native execution and coding-centric scope prevent full Deckent equivalence.

rows.name: Devin
rows.closest_because: Parallel sessions, MultiDevin, enterprise RBAC, VPC deployment, knowledge, schedules and MCP form a mature coding-fleet service.
rows.farther_because: Devin is the agent and hosted service; it does not govern an open fleet of heterogeneous third-party agents.

rows.name: Temporal
rows.closest_because: Durable workflows, immutable history, retries, signals, HITL and enterprise scale are a hard benchmark for Deckent's runtime.
rows.farther_because: Temporal is general durable-execution infrastructure; it has no agent operator product, evaluation flywheel or agent fleet UX by itself.

rows.name: n8n
rows.closest_because: Workflow automation, connectors, approvals and operations compete for some enterprise automation budgets.
rows.farther_because: Its core unit is a business workflow, not a governed software-agent attempt/evidence lifecycle.

rows.name: Untrivial Agent Orchestrator
rows.closest_because: Worktree fleets and PR/CI/review/merge loops overlap the engineering orchestration job.
rows.farther_because: Governance, verified settlement, learning and enterprise control-plane depth are limited.

rows.name: Replit Agent
rows.closest_because: End-to-end app building with full-environment checkpoints offers an excellent solo/basic user experience substitute.
rows.farther_because: It is a vertically integrated app-building cloud, not a neutral agent control plane.

rows.name: Hermes Agent
rows.closest_because: Terminal, gateway, tools and memory make Hermes a strong interaction and personal-agent runtime reference.
rows.farther_because: It lacks Deckent-scale organization governance, verified settlement and every-environment control-plane ambition.

rows.name: AutoGen
rows.closest_because: Event-driven multi-agent runtime, distributed workers and human feedback cover core orchestration patterns.
rows.farther_because: The application owner must define the behavior contract, governance and product surface.

rows.name: OpenHands
rows.closest_because: Open coding-agent runtime and hosted/enterprise options overlap execution and deployment.
rows.farther_because: It is principally an agent/runtime product, not a cross-agent evidence/governance operating system.

rows.name: Cursor + Windsurf
rows.closest_because: They dominate developer attention and can absorb basic agent supervision into the editor.
rows.farther_because: IDE-first agent UX does not provide Deckent's organization-wide multi-runtime authority and evidence chain.
